content:
maya: Heads-up: running into duplicate POSTs from the Android SDK when a coroutine cancels + OkHttp retry kicks in. Repro on emulator, flaky on device.

sam: ugh, can you paste the minimal repro? sounds like retryOnConnectionFailure resending non-idempotent calls.

maya: yep. minimal steps: 1) start sample app 2) trigger background network call (POST /checkout) 3) quickly background the app (or trigger cancellation) 4) network times out and our RetryInterceptor retries -> server sees 2 requests.

lucas: do you run with the SDK's default client config or custom? which okhttp version?

maya: default client + small custom interceptor to add auth header. OkHttp 4.11.0 on device, 4.10.0 on CI emulator. Noticed regression after bump to 4.11.0.

maya: sample config:```kotlin
val client = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .callTimeout(20, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
  .connectTimeout(5, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
  .retryOnConnectionFailure(true)
  .addInterceptor(AuthInterceptor())
  .build()
```

maya: our RetryInterceptor is naive: it catches IOException and re-executes the call. If coroutine cancelled while waiting, we still retry and re-enqueue network call. Log snippet:```
W/Network: call failed: java.io.InterruptedIOException: timeout
I/Retry: decision=retry, attempt=1
I/Network: sending request POST /checkout id=abcd1234
I/Network: sending request POST /checkout id=efgh5678
```

qa-ana: that looks bad. Could be OkHttp's dispatcher + coroutine cancellation race. Did you try checking call.isCanceled() before retry?

maya: I tried guard but the cancel check happens earlier and still replays. Repro: on emulator set network delay via adb to 3s then trigger cancellation after 1s. Observed duplicate requests ~30% of runs.

sam: can you share a tiny repro app? we can test locally. Even a snippet that uses CoroutineScope.launch { call.execute() } and then cancel scope quickly should repro.

maya: pushing a pared-down sample to the repro branch: https://git.internal/repro/android-retry-dup. Key bits attached here:```kotlin
suspend fun postCheckout(body: RequestBody) = withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
  val req = Request.Builder()
    .url(BASE + "/checkout")
    .post(body)
    .build()
  val call = client.newCall(req)
  try {
    val resp = call.execute()
    return@withContext resp
  } catch (e: IOException) {
    // naive retry
    call.clone().execute()
  }
}
```

lucas: cloning and executing after IOException without checking cancellation will definitely replay. OkHttp call.clone() returns a fresh Call; cancellation of original doesn't propagate.

maya: right. But our SDK previously relied on OkHttp's internal retry behavior. After the bump, the original call's timeout gets triggered slightly differently, so our catch happens after coroutine cancellation.

sam: short-term fix: treat POSTs as non-retriable unless idempotency-key present. Also add check: if (call.isCanceled || coroutineContext.isActive == false) { throw e } before retry.

qa-ana: can we add a global guard in the SDK to prevent retries on coroutine cancellation? Maybe a helper that wraps execute() and respects coroutine cancellation state.

lucas: yep. suggestion: use suspendCancellableCoroutine + call.enqueue(...) and link call.cancel() to continuation invokeOnCancellation. That way cancellation cancels the underlying call and prevents later manual retries. Example:```kotlin
suspend fun Call.await(): Response = suspendCancellableCoroutine { cont ->
  enqueue(object : Callback { ... onFailure { if (!cont.isCancelled) cont.resumeWithException(it) } ... })
  cont.invokeOnCancellation { cancel() }
}
```

maya: good idea. I'll try reworking our wrapper instead of naive execute() + retry. Also adding idempotency-key header for checkout as a belt-and-suspenders.

dev-bot: deployed test build to QA emulator fleet with idempotency header and cancellable call wrapper (build #312).

qa-ana: running 1000 fuzz runs on emulator build #312. Will report pass/fail rate in thread.

sam: long-term, we should add automated test in SDK CI that simulates coroutine cancellations under slow network and ensure no duplicate POSTs.

maya: agreed. Will open PR with changes + unit/integration test. Thanks for the quick triage :thumbsup:
